question.text: Let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></math> are the points on the argand plane which lie on the circle with equation <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced close="|" open="|" separators="|"><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>-</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow></mfenced><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>4</mn><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt></mfrac></math> (where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></math> is the centre of the circle). If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn></math> and <math><msub><mrow><mi>z</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><msub><mrow><mi>z</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo></math> then <math><mfenced close="|" open="|" separators="|"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">arg</mi></mrow><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi>z</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></mfenced></mrow></mrow></mrow></mfenced></math> is equal to (where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>arg</mi><mi>Z</mi><mo>∈</mo><mfenced close="]" separators="|"><mrow><mo>-</mo><mi>π</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>π</mi></mrow></mfenced></math>)

solution.text:
Here z1+z2+z33=z0⇒z3=4+3z0
Therefore, center coincides with the circumcentre
⇒ Triangle is equilateral ⇒z1-z2=4
Clearly, z3 either lie in the second or third quadrant

So the centre z0 also lies in the second or third quadrant.
∴z0 can be =-2+23i,-2-23i

⇒argz0=5π6,7π6
